patient_information: A 14-year-old girl from the Solomon Islands.
chief_complaint: A painless, non-healing large ulcer of her left leg.
history_of_present_illness: The ulcer began 1 month prior to presentation.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from the Solomon Islands, a region where yaws is still a common problem in the West Pacific.
physical_exam: A large lesion (approximately 3 cm diameter) covered by a layer of crust was present on the left lower leg, with a smaller, similar lesion lower down the leg; no regional lymphadenopathy or other skin or bone lesions were noted.
labs_and_diagnostics: A rapid plasma reagin (RPR) test was positive at a titre of 1:64.
differential_diagnosis: Other relevant differential diagnoses include pyoderma, tropical ulcer, cutaneous diphtheria, Aeromonas hydrophila infection, and Haemophilus ducreyi.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with a single intramuscular (IM) dose of benzathine benzylpenicillin (1.2 million units) and the skin lesion resolved over the next 10 days; 12 months later, she presented with a similar ulcer on the right leg, and a repeat RPR test was positive at 1:8, considered a cure from the previous treatment due to a greater than four-fold fall in titre.
final_diagnosis: Yaws, with a subsequent leg ulcer on the right leg interpreted to be of a different aetiology.
